findings.title: Frontend writing-craft LLM: api_key/base_url sent in POST body, not via headers
findings.description: analyzeWritingCraftLLM() spreads llmConfig (api_key, base_url, model) directly into POST body via `...llmConfig`. Unlike writing.ts which was fixed to use X-LLM-API-Key/X-LLM-Base-Url headers, this endpoint still transmits credentials in the request body.
findings.impact: API keys visible in server logs, proxy caches, and browser DevTools. Same vulnerability class as ISS-002 (partially resolved).
findings.suggestion: Extract api_key/base_url from llmConfig and pass via X-LLM-API-Key/X-LLM-Base-Url headers, matching the writing.ts fix pattern. Also update writing-craft-llm.ts backend to read from headers.

findings.title: graphAddEntity() accepts arbitrary entityType without validation
findings.description: graphAddEntity(entityType, name, properties) passes entityType directly to engine.createEntity() without calling validateEntityType(). The foreshadowPlantEndpoint hardcodes 'foreshadow', but any future caller could inject arbitrary labels. The graph service layer is the last line of defense.
findings.impact: If any endpoint or agent calls graphAddEntity with user-supplied entityType, Cypher label injection is possible.
findings.suggestion: Add validateEntityType(entityType) call inside graphAddEntity() before delegating to engine.createEntity(). This provides defense-in-depth even if callers forget to validate.

findings.title: graphQueryEndpoint passes raw Cypher from client to engine without validation
findings.description: graphQueryEndpoint directly forwards body.cypher to graphQuery(). While knowledgeUtils.ts validates entity types and escapes strings for merge/delete, the /graph/query endpoint accepts arbitrary Cypher. Frontend PersistedEntityTab constructs Cypher via buildGraphMergeMutation (safe), but the raw endpoint has no guard.
findings.impact: A compromised or misconfigured frontend could send destructive Cypher (DETACH DELETE, DROP, etc.) through /graph/query. Current frontend uses safe builders, but the endpoint itself has no defense.
findings.suggestion: Add a Cypher allowlist or at minimum block DETACH DELETE / DROP patterns at the graphQueryEndpoint level. This is a known design trade-off (flexibility vs safety) but should be documented and ideally guarded.

findings.title: Legacy route /writing-helper/process still registered alongside /writing/helper
findings.description: Both /writing-helper/process and /writing/helper map to writingHelperProcessEndpoint. The legacy route appears to be a backward-compat artifact from a route rename.
findings.impact: Two routes for the same handler increases maintenance surface. Client confusion about which to use.
findings.suggestion: Deprecate /writing-helper/process with a log warning, and schedule removal in next major version.

findings.title: Knowledge API module has mixed concerns: memory + graph + foreshadow + character depth
findings.description: knowledge.ts exports searchMemory, addMemory, uploadMemoryFile (memory API), queryGraph, getCharacter, getForeshadows (graph API), plantForeshadow, getForeshadowStats (foreshadow API), analyzeCharacterDepth, getCharacterProfile, getCharacterRelationships (character API). These are 4 distinct subsystems in one module.
findings.impact: High cognitive load per import. Any change to one subsystem risks breaking others. Makes tree-shaking less effective.
findings.suggestion: Split into memory.ts, graph.ts, foreshadow.ts, character-analysis.ts. The barrel export in client.ts already re-exports from knowledge.ts — update it.

findings.title: Frontend workspace parameter: 3 different append patterns across API modules
findings.description: Three different workspace-append functions: appendWorkspacePayload (knowledge, agents, writing), appendLegacyChatWorkspacePayload (chat), appendLegacyMemoryWorkspacePayload (memory). Each produces a different payload shape for the same conceptual 'workspace context'.
findings.impact: Backend must handle 3 different payload shapes. Risk of inconsistency when adding new workspace fields.
findings.suggestion: Unify into single appendWorkspacePayload with optional mode flags. Legacy shapes should be phased out.

findings.title: Foreshadow/Character analysis frontend APIs don't pass workspace context
findings.description: plantForeshadow(), getForeshadowStats(), analyzeCharacterDepth(), getCharacterProfile(), getCharacterRelationships() do not accept or forward workspace context. Meanwhile, the backend graph endpoints do support scope filtering via resolveGraphScope().
findings.impact: In multi-workspace scenarios, these calls return unfiltered data (all workspaces mixed together). Scope filtering exists in backend but is not exercised by frontend.
findings.suggestion: Add workspace parameter to these API calls, matching the pattern used by queryGraph() and getCharacter().

findings.title: Story Bible API _workspace parameter declared but unused
findings.description: All sb* functions declare _workspace?: ProjectWorkspaceContext but never use it — the parameter is prefixed with underscore indicating intentionally unused. The backend story-bible-endpoints.ts does support workspace scoping.
findings.impact: Story Bible data is not scoped to workspace in frontend calls. Same as ARCH-004 pattern.
findings.suggestion: Wire _workspace parameter into callApi payloads via appendWorkspacePayload, matching knowledge.ts patterns.

findings.title: analyzeWritingCraftLLM: LLMConfig spreads into body including api_key/base_url (also SEC-001)
findings.description: The spread `...llmConfig` into the body payload means api_key and base_url are sent in the request body, but the backend writing-craft-llm.ts also reads from headers. This means the body fields work as fallback but are not the preferred path.
findings.impact: Functional but not secure. Works today because backend reads body as fallback, but deprecated path.
findings.suggestion: Refactor to header-based transmission as in writing.ts. Mark body fields @deprecated in LLMConfig type.

findings.title: foreshadowPlantEndpoint doesn't validate workspace scoping
findings.description: foreshadowPlantEndpoint calls graphAddEntity('foreshadow', ...) without workspace scope. The created entity has no workspaceId/projectId, so it becomes a 'legacy' (unscoped) entity that pollutes other workspaces' views.
findings.impact: Foreshadow entities created via /foreshadow/plant are visible across all workspaces (no isolation).
findings.suggestion: Resolve workspace scope from request body (like graphQueryEndpoint does) and pass to graphAddEntity, or include workspaceId in properties.

findings.title: Story Bible sbGetEntity uses GET with path parameter but entityId is not URL-encoded
findings.description: `callApi('/story-bible/entity/${entityId}', 'GET')` — if entityId contains special characters (/, #, ?), the URL will be malformed. Other GET endpoints like sbDeleteEntity have the same pattern.
findings.impact: Entities with IDs containing URL-unsafe characters will fail to load or delete.
findings.suggestion: Use encodeURIComponent(entityId) in URL interpolation, matching the pattern in m10-apis.ts styleProfile.

findings.title: chatStream SSE parser does not handle multiline data fields
findings.description: The SSE parser in chatStream splits on newlines and processes event/data pairs per line. If a data field spans multiple lines (valid SSE per spec), only the first line is captured. The writing.ts consumeSseWritingEvents has the same pattern.
findings.impact: Malformed or multi-line SSE data is truncated. In practice, the backend sends single-line JSON so this rarely triggers.
findings.suggestion: Accumulate data lines until an empty line signals event completion, per SSE specification.
